Hi Priya — thanks for sending this over and for the clear callouts. I answered the attached sheet inline and summarized our responses below to make procurement easier. Copying Neha (security ops) and Ben (sales manager) for visibility on SLA/contract items.

Summary answers (hosted API):
- Region-scoped retention: Yes. We support tenant-scoped residency selection at account onboarding (us, eu, apac). For hosted API customers that require EU-only retention, we pin data to EU regions for processing and storage and apply region-only backups.
- Deletion timeline: For primary data stores, we purge user-provided data within 30 days of an account erasure request. For backups, we apply a standard backup reaping window up to 90 days; if a customer requests immediate expunge we can apply an accelerated retention sweep (subject to contract) — see note on exceptions below.
- Legal hold: We can suspend automated deletion workflows for specific tenant IDs for an agreed period. Holds are logged and require a signed request from an authorized customer contact. Holds can be maintained beyond the default retention windows (we typically support up to 12 months by default; longer with an admin-level agreement).

Notes and evidence we attached:
- redwood-hostedapi-dataflow-v2.pdf (diagram showing region pinning, backups, and deletion flows)
- Residency & retention FAQ link: https://docs.redwood.ai/security/hosted-api-data-lifecycle

Exceptions/contract items to flag to procurement:
- Immediate backup purges (sub-30 day) are treated as managed services (operational change) and are outside standard hosted SLA; there is typically a small one-time fee and a change-control window.
- Highly-restricted geofencing with dedicated physical isolation requires Redwood Dedicated or Private (VPC) — hosted customers can get region pinning but not physical isolation guarantees.

I attached a concise one-page PDF that Argent can include with the questionnaire. Ben — if Argent asks for a commercial exception for backup purge timing, can we confirm permissible credits/ops SLA?

Thanks,
Karthik

Hi Priya — quick follow-up with the specific language you can paste into vendor risk. I've kept each point short for ease of ingestion.

1) Backup cross-region replication (EU-pinned tenants):
- Statement: "For tenants pinned to EU regions, Redwood does not replicate primary customer data to non-EU regions for routine backups or processing. Backups for EU-pinned tenants are stored in EU-only snapshots that are encrypted and access-controlled. Cross-region restore to non-EU environments is prohibited except for court-ordered or lawful-transfer situations and only after legal review and written customer notification."

2) Customer-initiated backup purge process & SLA:
- Process: Customer submits a signed data expunge request (form provided) from an authorized admin contact. Redwood logs the request, schedules an accelerated backup sweep, and provides a purge evidence package (job ids + timestamps).
- SLA: Standard hosted purge window is up to 90 days. Expedited purge (sub-30 day) is available as a billable managed-service option; typical ops window is 7–21 days depending on dataset size and retention tier.
- Who signs: Authorized customer admin (name & email) plus the original account owner on file.

3) Audit trail for deletion requests:
- Retention: Deletion-request audit logs (request metadata, operator IDs, job ids, timestamps) are retained for 12 months by default for operational traceability. Logs contain metadata only (requestor identity, tenant ID, operation result); they do not contain customer content payloads.

4) Legal hold capabilities:
- We support tenant-scoped holds that suspend automated purges. Holds are recorded, cannot be silently removed, and can be extended with a signed agreement. Default supported hold duration is 12 months; longer durations can be arranged with contractual amendments.

I'll attach the brief PDF with the above text for your vendor portal. If Argent wants to add an expedited purge as a line item in procurement, Ben is copied to follow up on pricing/credits.

Best,
